result.rationale: Diff shows zoho-bigin calling refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId) while the function signature is (refreshFunction, appSlug, userId) and every other integration passes credential.userId. The value becomes calcomUserId in the sync request, so the credential row id would be sent as a user identifier, breaking the sync lookup. Verifiable from the diff.

judged_text: zoho-bigin passes credentialId (the credential row's id) as the userId parameter of refreshOAuthTokens, which becomes the calcomUserId sent to the sync endpoint. In sharing mode the parent application receives the credential's row id as the user identifier, looks up the wrong user (or none), and returns the wrong user's tokens or a 404 — Bigin refresh breaks, and if the parent does return tokens they are synced against the wrong account.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new call `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes `credentialId` as the third argument, but `refreshOAuthTokens` treats that argument as the *Cal.com userId* and sends it as `calcomUserId` to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` (`refreshOAuthTokens.ts`: `calcomUserId: userId.toString()`). Other integrations consistently pass `credential.userId` (e.g., Zoom/O365/Webex). Using a `credentialId` value here will misidentify the user at the sync endpoint and can break token refresh or sync tokens to the wrong account when sharing mode is enabled.
